To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
axillary lymph node scintigraphy using 111In‐liposomes is a sensitive and specific test that may be useful as an adjunct to other methods of staging breast cancer patients.
axillary lymph node scanning is a useful tool in the evaluation of breast cancer.
the pre‐operative detection of axilary lymph node metastases by isotope imaging is feasible and may be of value.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a noninvasive technique of preoperatively assessing axillary lymph nodes in patients with breast cancer, with the ultimate objective of reducing the morbidity of the axillary staging operation.
the preoperative evaluation of the axilla in breast cancer by axillary lymphoscitigraphy.
the detection of breast cancer metastases in the axillary lymph nodes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of liposome‐labelled 99Tcm for lymphoscintigraphy in patients with breast carcinoma is feasible, but that the accuracy of this technique in predicting the status of axillary lymph nodes is not yet established.
the results of this preliminary study are encouraging, but not conclusive.

the technique of lymphoscintigraphy is a useful adjunctive procedure for the evaluation of the axilla in breast cancer, but it is not a substitute for the surgical evaluation of the axillary lymph node status.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of liposome‐based lymphoscintigraphy is a promising method for the preoperative detection of the presence of lymph node metastasis.
axillary lymph node scanning with 99Tcm labelled liposome appears to be a useful adjunct to the evaluation of axillary lymph nodes in breast cancer.
axillary lymph node mapping and lymphoscintigraphy can provide useful information in breast cancer staging, and that the procedure is safe and easy to perform, with a low rate of complications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
axillary lymph node status is the most powerful predictor of survival and is the single most important factor in the management of patients with breast cancer.
axillary lymph node dissection can be omitted in the presence of normal axillary lymph node images.
axillary lymphosintigraphy is a useful tool for detecting the spread of breast cancer.
